changelog:
The fix for Plex rejecting the sign-in.

**Plex**
- Adding a server works. The app was sending the account token — the one that
  signs you in to plex.tv — to the server itself, and a Plex server wants its own
  per-server token instead. Everything before that step succeeded, which is why
  the sign-in and the server list looked fine and only the import failed.
- The token is now re-registered on every refresh and after every restart, not
  only when the source is added. Without that, a Plex source would have imported
  once and then failed silently after the app was next killed, with posters
  quietly falling back to placeholder tiles.
- A server whose only working route is Plex's relay is now reported as exactly
  that, instead of "unreachable". The difference matters: unreachable means no
  route, relay-only means there is one and it is too slow for video — and that
  one you can fix with Remote Access or port forwarding.
- A server that answers with a temporary error, rather than not answering, now
  counts as reachable. It was being skipped.
- If adding a server still fails, the message now says which credential was
  used, whether a token was attached at all, whether Plex offered a per-server
  token, and whether the server is owned by your account. No part of any token
  appears in it.

**Still not proven**
- Playing a Plex item has never succeeded. Nothing has reached that point yet.

Known limits: multi-view, picture-in-picture, DVR and recording are not in this
build. Catch-up still has not been tested against a real provider archive.
